# Synthetic Copied Scaffold

[Synthetic copied scaffold core claim — support: argument]

The [shared lifecycle method](../../../chapters/living-book-methodology.qmd#shared-chapter-lifecycle-method)
is the declared common owner.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["Declared purpose and bounded authority"] --> B["Versioned chapter-specific contract"]
  B["Versioned chapter-specific contract"] --> C["Admission and boundary checks"]
  C["Admission and boundary checks"] --> D["Execute with complete lineage and denominators"]
  D["Execute with complete lineage and denominators"] --> E["Observe outcomes, costs, and residuals"]
  E["Observe outcomes, costs, and residuals"] --> F{"Independent checks pass?"}
  F -- "no" --> G["Quarantine, narrow, correct, or stop"]
  F -- "yes" --> H["Versioned bounded handoff"]
```

## Interfaces and ownership boundary

The chapter says that it owns a distinct control plane, but it does not identify
the object or decision that neighboring owners cannot preserve.

## Evidence and falsification program

A fair test must freeze the mechanism, authority, comparator set, tuning and
rescue budgets, metrics, stopping rule, and protected holdout before outcomes
are visible.

## Codex test plan

| Test | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Contract completeness | Reject missing identity, authority, scope, version, consumer, residual, or expiry fields. | planned |
| Boundary mutation | Substitute an adjacent owner's authority and require rejection. | planned |
| Failure-family mutation | Inject at least one mechanism-specific failure and preserve the full attempt denominator. | planned |
| No-promotion control | Ensure prose, schemas, fixtures, and source-reported results cannot promote the chapter core claim. | planned |

## Handoff

The next chapter consumes this chapter's bounded outputs without inheriting
authority, certainty, or support that this chapter did not establish.
